findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify that the per-call record's `llm_calls` field is a synthetic constant (always 1, derived by the accumulator, not read from `runner._extract_usage`) since `_extract_usage` only exposes `requests`, not `llm_calls`.
evidence: runner.py:699-708: `_extract_usage` returns `{input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, requests}` — no `llm_calls` key
Plan text: 'usage is recorded per CALL as {criteria: [ids the call covered], llm_calls, requests, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens}'
The plan also states 'llm_calls/requests count in full for each covered criterion' — treating llm_calls as a separate field, not derivable from `requests`
findings.finding: The plan specifies a per-call usage record schema that includes a `llm_calls` field — `{criteria, llm_calls, requests, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens}` — but `runner._extract_usage` (runner.py:699-708), the sole source of the `_usage` dict, produces only `{input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, requests}`. There is no `llm_calls` key in the runner's output; it would have to be a synthetic field added by the accumulator (always 1 per call record). The plan never acknowledges this derivation, treating `llm_calls` as if it already flows from the runner.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Aggregation protocol' / 'usage is recorded per CALL as {criteria: [ids...], llm_calls, requests, ...}'
scenarios: An implementer reading the plan adds a `llm_calls` key read from `result['_usage']` and finds it absent — must derive it as a constant 1 per record, which is undocumented

The AC test for 'coverage.metrics contains input/output/cache token totals' passes, but a test asserting the per-call record schema has `llm_calls` silently fails or requires unspecified derivation logic
findings.suggested_fix: In the Aggregation protocol, add: 'The `llm_calls` field on each call record is set to 1 (one LLM call per record — it is synthetic, not from `_extract_usage`); `requests` reflects the agentic request-cycle count from the runner's _usage dict.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how usage from context-limit-raising runner.run calls is captured (e.g. attach `partial_usage` to the raised exception, or add a usage-capture callback/contextvar in runner.run that is readable even on failure) so the 'billed is billed' invariant holds for ladder retries.
evidence: runner.py:412: `usage: dict[str, int] = {}`  — initialized before try block
runner.py:543: `result['_usage'] = usage`  — only executed on SUCCESS, after the try block
runner.py:461-497: LLMError and generic Exception paths raise WITHOUT attaching usage to the exception

sizing.py:pass1_with_ladder:322: `except Exception as exc: if not is_context_limit_error(exc): return []` — a context-limit exception is caught and re-entered into the ladder WITHOUT a _usage return value being available
ABSENCE: no mechanism in the plan or runner to attach usage to the raised exception object
findings.finding: The plan's invariant 'retry usage is never discarded (billed is billed)' is unachievable for the context-limit-exception path via the current runner API: when pass1_with_ladder's batch call raises a context-limit exception, runner.run raises BEFORE executing `result['_usage'] = usage` (runner.py:543), so there is no _usage dict on the exception object and no return value to harvest. The plan specifies no mechanism (e.g., attaching partial usage to the exception, or a usage-capture callback in runner.run) to collect the failed attempt's billed tokens.
findings.location: Approach section: 'Ladder retries: every attempt pass1_with_ladder makes for a chunk — including escalation retries after a context-limit error — appends its own call record (billed is billed; retry usage is never discarded)'
scenarios: A batch call hits the context-limit; the tokens that triggered the limit are billed by the provider but never captured in any call record — the plan's 'billed is billed' invariant is silently violated.
A model-escalation retry also hits context-limit before the largest model; those intermediate billed attempts are also lost.
findings.suggested_fix: In runner.run, attach the partial `usage` dict to the exception before re-raising (e.g. `exc.partial_usage = usage`), and update pass1_with_ladder's except blocks to read `getattr(exc, 'partial_usage', {})` and append a call record with those partial tokens.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Explicitly specify the changed future-collection loop pattern in run_pass1 (e.g. destructure `findings_part, usage_part = fu.result()` and accumulate separately) so the implementer knows both the _chunk return-type change AND the consuming loop must change atomically.
evidence: pass1.py:486-501: `with ThreadPoolExecutor(...) as ex: ... for fu in st_futs + ag_futs: findings.extend(fu.result() or [])`

ABSENCE: the plan describes _chunk's new return shape and run_pass1's aggregate derivation but does not state the changed loop pattern (e.g. `fs, u = fu.result(); findings.extend(fs); usage_records.append(u)`)
Plan Approach: 'run_pass1 derives (a) the aggregate sum over all call records' — without specifying the thread-pool collection mechanism
findings.finding: The plan does not specify the result-collection pattern for concurrent _chunk futures after the return-type change. Currently pass1.py:490 does `findings.extend(fu.result() or [])`, which works because fu.result() is a list. After the change, fu.result() is a (list, dict) tuple — `findings.extend(tuple)` would add two items (the list and the dict) to findings instead of extending with the findings list. The plan says _chunk 'accumulates usage' but doesn't describe the changed destructuring in the main-thread future-collection loop.
findings.location: Approach section: 'run_pass1 derives (a) the aggregate sum over all call records'; pass1.py:486-501 (ThreadPoolExecutor fan-out result collection loop)
scenarios: If the future-collection loop is not updated alongside _chunk's return type, findings.extend(fu.result()) silently corrupts the findings list by adding the usage dict as a finding-level entry.
A test that checks findings count would catch this, but the plan's tests focus on usage values, not findings list integrity.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach section: 'In run_pass1's future-collection loop, each `fu.result()` is destructured as `(findings_part, usage_part) = fu.result()` — `findings.extend(findings_part)` and `call_records.append(usage_part)` — replacing the current `findings.extend(fu.result() or [])`'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify whether call-record accumulation is thread/coroutine-safe: either specify that each chunk call *returns* its records (merged post-hoc by the caller, inherently race-free) or name the synchronization primitive (e.g., `threading.Lock`, `asyncio.Queue`) protecting the shared list.
evidence: Plan says 'appends its own call record' without specifying the data structure is thread/coroutine-safe or that records are returned and merged post-hoc.
T9 checklist: 'Shared/mutable state mutated atomically (lock/CAS/transaction, no check-then-act TOCTOU); operation idempotent under retry/at-least-once.'
ABSENCE: no mention of a lock, queue, thread-local accumulation, or return-and-merge pattern for the per-chunk records list.
findings.finding: The plan specifies that pass1_with_ladder 'appends its own call record' for each chunk attempt, but does not address whether this accumulator is safe for concurrent access. Production batch runners typically process chunks in parallel (threads or async tasks); if multiple chunks write to a shared call-records list simultaneously, there is a check-then-act / lost-update race that silently drops usage data.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Ladder retries: every attempt pass1_with_ladder makes for a chunk … appends its own call record'; also production_batch_runner.py (batch execution model)
scenarios: Two chunks finish near-simultaneously in a thread-pool executor; both append to the same list, Python list.append is GIL-safe but async task interleaving is not — if the runner is async, a coroutine could yield mid-append logic, dropping one record.

A ladder retry on chunk A runs concurrently with chunk B's first attempt; both append to the shared accumulator, potentially producing duplicate or missing entries if the accumulator is reassigned rather than mutated.
findings.suggested_fix: Have pass1_with_ladder return its call records as part of its return value (alongside findings and usage), and have run_pass1 merge all per-chunk record lists after awaiting/collecting all chunk results. This eliminates shared mutable state entirely and is the simplest correct approach.

findings.finding: The attribution rule for container calls (pass1_container) is unspecified. The plan distinguishes exactly two cases — 'AGENT call (single criterion)' and 'multi-criterion single-turn chunk' — but container calls are AGENTIC (execution_mode='agentic', confirmed at passes.py:428) AND multi-criterion (covering G3/G4/decomp-shape simultaneously). They fit neither rule as stated: the AGENT rule requires a single criterion; the multi-criterion rule specifies single-turn. An implementer must guess whether to (a) treat a container call as a multi-criterion AGENT call and divide token fields equally across G3/G4/decomp-shape, (b) apply the AGENT rule treating the criteria list as the single attribution unit, or (c) use a third unspecified rule.
